drug_class: Alpha-hydroxy acid / Skin moisturizer and exfoliant
purpose: Lactic acid is used to treat dry, rough, or scaly skin conditions such as dry skin, ichthyosis, and keratosis pilaris. It helps soften and smooth the skin by removing dead skin cells and boosting moisture. It can also help with minor skin irritation and flaking.
how_it_works: Lactic acid is a natural acid that gently loosens and removes the dead outer layer of skin cells, which helps your skin feel softer and smoother. It also helps your skin hold onto water, keeping it hydrated and moisturized. Think of it like a gentle exfoliator that also acts as a sponge for moisture in your skin.
common_side_effects: Mild stinging, burning, or itching when first applied, especially on sensitive or irritated skin. You may also notice mild redness or peeling as your skin adjusts. These effects usually lessen over time as your skin gets used to the product.
warnings: Avoid getting this product in your eyes, nose, or mouth. Do not apply to broken, cracked, or severely irritated skin. Your skin may become more sensitive to sunlight while using lactic acid, so use sunscreen and limit sun exposure. Talk to your doctor before using this if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. Stop using and contact your doctor if you notice severe burning, rash, or swelling.
typical_dosing: Apply a thin layer to the affected skin area once or twice daily, or as directed by your doctor or the product label. Gently rub it in until fully absorbed. Wash your hands after applying unless your hands are the area being treated.
